title: Men Dying Young: It Stops Now
summary: A Movember video on men's physical and mental health: real toughness means facing health problems early, rejecting industries that sell men self-destruction (tobacco, alcohol, PEDs), and reaching out for emotional support. He reveals that his father, grandfather and great-grandfather all died of prostate cancer that screening could have caught, while his uncle, who got checked early, became a grandfather.
claims: Men die on average about five years younger than women, and most of the causes are environmental and choice-driven rather than biological destiny
Ignoring signs of declining health is not toughness but cowardice; a true warrior wants to live long enough to fight a hundred battles
Health problems grow when ignored: something fixable in a week today can take ten months later or become incurable, and the anxiety of avoiding it is worse than the fix
Fitness and media culture sells men self-destruction (drinking, smoking, PEDs) as masculine, a strategy driven by tobacco, alcohol and drug interests; masculinity should be anti-consumerist
Men in their 20s should take advice from older men with families rather than peers or man-child influencers; the values you adopt in your 20s set the trajectory of your life

Health basics are simple and in your control: sleep, cut toxins (caffeine, drugs, alcohol), resistance training, and stay at a reasonably low body fat; thyroid hacks, infrared lights and enemas are bogus
Longevity correlates with physical activity and resistance training
Get bloodwork about twice a year plus dentist and general checkups; most early male deaths come from ignoring these
Prostate cancer is the second most common cancer in men, roughly a 10% lifetime risk, and about 9 in 10 cases are easily treatable if caught early
Start prostate screening in your 50s, or late 40s if of African descent, since Black men have twice the risk of dying from it

His great-grandfather (70), grandfather (60s) and father (50s, three years ago) all died of prostate cancer; his father avoided doctors out of fear and was diagnosed at stage three once it had spread to the bones
His uncle from the same bloodline got checked in his 30s, had problems caught early, and is now in his 70s and a grandfather
Advanced prostate cancer treatment kills testosterone, which means losing muscle and often depression
Steroids are androgenic and can bring on prostate cancer decades earlier in men genetically at risk, such as himself
PED use is selfish risk-taking that jeopardizes a man's ability to be a father and husband; he refuses to sabotage his health for a few gains
Men commit suicide about four times as often as women; many go months without being touched by a loved one, and isolation erodes mental health
Stoicism means controlling emotions after accepting them, not repressing them; repressed feelings drive behavior from the unconscious and often come out as anger
Reaching out for help (friends, family, therapy, groups, hotlines) is not weakness; mental distress, like cancer, is easier to treat early
